final_message:
The fix works correctly. The issue was that the original regex pattern `[^a-z0-9]+` matched all non-alphanumeric characters including spaces and punctuation, which caused multiple dashes when there were consecutive non-alphanumeric characters like the comma and spaces in "Hello,  World!".

The new implementation uses `re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text)` which replaces each sequence of one or more non-alphanumeric characters with a single hyphen, resulting in `'hello-world'` for the input `'Hello,  World!'`.
